options.denominator: Total clock-hours across the 5,094 calendar days from 2012-07-01 through 2026-06-11 (10 night or 14 daytime hours per date)
options.reason: A careful analyst may choose this framing to compare collision frequency while accounting for the unequal lengths of the night and daytime periods.
options.answer: These records cannot establish whether night is more dangerous per trip or mile because traffic exposure is not recorded; they show 10.97 reported crashes per clock-hour during night versus 23.98 during daytime, averaged across the date range.

options.metric: People injured and killed per reported crash
options.denominator: Total reported crashes in each period, expressed per 100 crashes
options.reason: A careful analyst may choose this framing to compare the human toll per collision, including both nonfatal injuries and deaths.
options.answer: These records cannot establish whether night is more dangerous per trip or mile because traffic exposure is not recorded; per 100 reported crashes, night had 40.45 people injured and 0.308 killed, compared with 31.01 injured and 0.111 killed by day.

options.metric: Share of reported crashes with injured or killed people
options.denominator: Total reported crashes in each period
options.reason: A careful analyst may choose this framing to show how often a reported crash involved casualties, independently of how many people were harmed in each crash.
options.answer: These records cannot establish whether night is more dangerous per trip or mile because traffic exposure is not recorded; 28.51% of night crashes involved at least one injury or death versus 23.50% of daytime crashes, while fatal crashes were 0.290% versus 0.108%.
